records.currentEnglish: The footlocker slowly creaks open.  Sand and water seem to be its only contents. But wait!  A small crab scurries out with a clue to the treasure in his claws!

Another one of Eitrigg's recruits, hm?

A sorry state of affairs we find ourselves in if this is the best the Horde can produce.  No matter.  By the time we think you're ready to leave the Valley, you'll be a proud warrior of the Horde.
The carapace of a scorpid isn't so thick that the strength of a determined <class> will be deterred. Strike strongly and without doubt, and the scorpids should prove easy prey.
We just, uh, need to adjust our dig site and we can get this whole thing back on track!

Our tools!

When the troggs overran the camp, we had to leave most of our tools behind. This'll be a big help once we get this invasion under control and can start working again!
Welcome to my fire, traveler.

Extra firewood? That is always welcome. It will keep these old bones warm through the cold nights of the Glades.

I have a sling for collecting wood myself, so you might as well hang onto that basket.
It is good to see you again! Are you here to trade?

Oh, these are wonderful. It is a shame to resort to violence with such majestic animals, but it is important to keep the roads safe, and these pelts will make beautiful blankets and shawls.

Here, let me give you something to remember them. It is both soft and sturdy.
We will finally have resolution to this mystery, and the animals will have peace at last!

This has been a long journey, <name>, but it was worth it.

At long last, you have wrested away the rod that the naga use to compel the sea creatures into their service. I will make sure it is destroyed, and the threshers and sea turtles can finally live in peace.

Thank you again. Your persistence has finally been rewarded, and I, personally, am grateful to you.
Mastery of the light will return, in time.

Pain is nothing new to those who have endured death, and as such the Forsaken are particularly hardy to it. Pain has a purifying property as well that you should embrace as a badge of honor and evidence that you are, in fact, still a servant of the light despite your new circumstances. 

Be well and walk in the light once more, <class>.

Tragically, more than a few of our brothers and sisters succumb to a similar madness after being risen. As precious as every Forsaken soul is, sometimes the best we can do is grant those that cannot acclimate a clean end.

I will say a prayer to the light for her. Thank you for doing what must be done, <name>.

Welcome aboard, <class>. It's always encouraging to see more of our number roaming these lands. There are many here in Brill in need of assistance from adventurers such as yourself. Seek employment and grow stronger in the light. Return to me whenever you need training. 

When you've proven yourself to myself and the people of Brill, I will provide guidance for the next leg of your journey.

Go with the light, <class>.
Another fresh recruit? Welcome to Tyr's Watch, brother.

We appreciate the assistance. I'm sure this won't stop the attacks entirely, but it'll hopefully slow them down a bit. It's hard enough rebuilding this place without a murloc trying to stab you in the back with a spear.
Welcome to Bandarion Keep, <class>. It's always good to see a new face.

Breton sent you up here, eh? Excellent.

My name is Danitha Morr, and I am the closest thing this keep has to a commander. If you come seeking fellowship amongst those that still remain loyal to the light, you've come to the right place.

There's a lot of work to do here before we can fully establish ourselves, and we'd be most appreciative if you would be willing to lend aid.

They say location is everything. While this fortress may look imposing perched upon these bluffs, it's turning out to be quite the challenge to stay supplied this far from proper civilization. An unfortunate oversight on our part.

I'm glad to see that your trip to Shadowvale bore fruit. I'll send Breton and a few of the other new recruits over later to clear the rest of the cellar out and retrieve anything left down in the dark.

The Tarnished threaten what little goodwill we have with the other Forsaken. As much as it pains me to cross blades with our former brothers and sisters, they must be stopped if our fledgling order is to survive.

Excellent work, <name>. Every time one of these Tarnished strike out and kill one of the Forsaken, it becomes that much easier for our detractors to stoke mistrust towards us paladins. Eliminating them will help further our cause and solidify our place here in Tirisfal.

I suspect it may take a long time for us to be fully embraced by the Forsaken and the horde. It could take years... or maybe even decades, but the best we can do is keep trying to prove ourselves.
Let me know when you are finished, so I can try to calibrate my instruments again.
Well done, my friend. Let me try my calibrations again...
Let me know when you are finished, so I can try to calibrate my instruments again.
It seems like everything is working properly. Thank you, <name>.
Did you find the supplies?
Oh, that's a relief! It looks like it's all here. Thank you!
Have you been to the mine yet?
Oh, very nice. Do you see that shine? Truly, they don't make them like they used to.
Did you find the supplies?
You look a bit damp, <name>. Sorry about that. But thank you for retrieving the supplies.
A strong scent of apples burns your nose as you inspect the device.
The machine dispenses a clear liquid into a bottle...
The sergeant's eyes light up as he notices your bottle of Thunder Applejack...

Do my eyes deceive me? I haven't seen a drop of Thunder Applejack in months!
This should put a smile on the troops' faces. You have my thanks, <class>!
Yes?
We lost two members of the watch last week to the murlocs, <class>. Hopefully with their leader slain, we can start pushing them out of Elwynn.
What's that you got there? It looks like one of my books.

Hey! How did you end up with that? It's supposed to be on the shelf! Oh dear, the kobolds have been stealing my books again. They must want to eat them!

Thanks for bringing back the book, but what will I do about the rest of my missing collection?
Have you rescued my books yet, <name>?!

Thank you so much! Here! Take one of these how-to books. I don't need them.

But there are still so many books missing. The kobolds don't seem to be eating them. So, why do they want them?
Kobolds with books? Yah, I've seen kobolds running back and forth with books, yelling at each other. They must be stealing them from the library inside the abbey.
Yes?

So, you took down Elmpaw? Very impressive, <name>!

Let me give you something in return for your trophy - I know a few collectors who will pay quite well to have this on their mantle once I've prepared it.
Any luck with those wolf pelts?
Excellent work collecting these pelts, <class>. You have a real talent for hunting.
Have you retrieved those stolen books yet?

Thank you for returning these stolen books, <name>. I'll get them back to Brother Paxton at once.

You're becoming quite the hero around here. Great job!
What have your studies revealed?
Theory and practice are two sides of a coin, <name>. Remember this.
I can help ye' track down this varmint. Let me whip somethin' up for ye'.
Have you figured out where the Kobolds are heading?

What's this, <name>? Tracking kobolds?

Well, of course they're headed toward the Fargodeep mine! That place is infested with kobolds.

Good work, I guess. I'm going to need someone to take care of that problem.
Have you found all the books yet?

I applaud your diligence, <name>. Brother Paxton sent a list of books, and you've found most of the missing ones. The rest must have been taken to the Jasperlode Mine.

You can keep that book bag!
Have you found all my missing books yet?
Oh, <name>! Thank you so much for saving my library. You've done me an amazing service. Please take one of these fine weapons. They were intended for the militia, but you can make better use of them.
Oh. You're back?

The potion didn't work? Of course it didn't work. You brought me insufficient hearts. The recipe clearly calls for six. You brought three.

However, I confess I hadn't considered applications for murloc parts until now...

<Renferrel takes the eyes.>

I can afford to sacrifice a few of my own hearts to get your Deathstalker's strength back.
You return! I was beginning to come to terms with devolving into a ghoul.

<Quinn takes the potion and drinks it.>

Yes, I can feel it working. I will soon be able to travel.

You have done me a great favor, <name>.
'Ello again! Did you bring back alchemy stuff?

Oh my gosh! Look at these! Did you pick the herbs yourself?

Wow, thanks mister, I am going to see what I can make with these right now! Do you want to watch?
Don't worry about me, I'm a big girl. I can take care of myself. Just don't tell anyone I am hiding here, it's our little secret.

You brought me murloc eyes! I am so excited for my first REAL potion I can't breathe!

I snuck out and grabbed a few more herbs while you were away and found some empty vials downstairs. Um... you can do the mixing this time.

<The child watches enthusiastically you mix the ingredients, but her nose crumples as you add the eyes. The concoction takes on a sickly orange in mere seconds.>

Wow! See, I was right. I wouldn't drink that, but here's my recipe if you wanted to make more. Come back sometime!

Yah, I overheard. I warned Brother Paxton three times about the kobolds tunneling under the abbey.

It looks like the kobolds have taken a lot of books. There are whole bookshelves emptied out. You should probably see what Brother Paxton wants you to do about it.

While you're here, can I talk to you about tradeskills? I'd be happy to answer any questions you have, or point you toward the local trainers.
Such pests cannot be allowed to find root in our peaceful grove. An infestation can quickly grow dangerous if left unchecked.
Cirrusflies aren't to be underestimated. They might not seem dangerous, but you have to watch out for the bigger ones. The bigger they are, the meaner!

The Al'Aketh cult represents the most direct and urgent danger to our homeland. Their increasingly extremist actions have destabilized our society and damaged our already-weakened connection to the spirits of the four winds. The elements demand action to prove our resilience and resolve, which are traits that are endemic to the domain of the element of earth.
You have returned and brought what I have requested and thus your grit and determination are unquestionable. You are ready for the next step, <name>.

Ah... <name>... child of the four winds... You seek understanding. You seek answers. Why have the winds left you? How may you get them back? These are answers I cannot provide, for I do not know the motives or movements of the winds.

I can, however, teach you much of the earth. Its strength, its resolve. Even here, high in this endless sea of clouds, you are still a creature of the earth. If you hope to find the strength to speak to the spirits of the four winds once more, this is the path you must walk.

As you will come to learn, the path we walk is not as simple as it may seem. While we seek to find the voice needed to speak with the spirits of the winds, the winds are but one of the elemental forces of this world. Only through understanding, and--we hope--mastery of all four elements will we regain our voice to again sing the songs of the wind.

Good!

The totem I will craft for you is more than a symbol of your status among <class>--it has abilities beyond that. One use of the totem is as a focus for spells. Those spells are tied to the earth, and as you earn greater and greater wisdom, more of the earth's abilities will be made accessible to you.

The trainers will know when you are ready for greater knowledge.

But for now, take this earth totem...
Using your ability to walk on air can get you out of--and, well... into--all kinds of trouble!

Ah, ye got me letter, <name>... good.

Time was when ye'd not catch a <race> dead wit' a bow in their hand--no more, I guess. It's good for Stormwind, but bad for the kobolds and man eatin' beasts in the area.

Get yerself squared away, learn the lay o' the land, and come back to me whenever you need training. I'll be here night or day.

This land is grown' more dangerous, and as ye meet other folk, I think ye'll find they all have problems they could use some help with--help a skilled <class> can give 'em. Good luck.
Greetings, <name>. I'm pleased to have the privilege of furthering your magical studies.

Let me have a look at you. Yes, I believe you will make a fine young <class>. The power of the arcane has waned amongst our people, but there are those who would seek to rediscover much of what we've lost in the millennia we've spent here amongst the clouds. I am sure that you will lead the charge in this never ending search for arcane knowledge, and ultimately make us proud.

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps.
<Tai'ree nods at you curtly.>

The way of the <class> is fraught with danger, and only those with the keenest senses and quickest reflexes can thrive in the wilds. I look at you and I am reminded of myself when I stood before my mentor, so many years ago. I believe that you have what it takes, but in the end that is up to you alone.

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps.
<Akeri eyes you suspiciously.>

I almost did not hear you approach me, young <class>.

Almost.

Almost won't be good enough when you leave Thendal Grove. You must be a slender blade, silent and steady. Ever vigilant and ever mindful of your surroundings. You might have what it takes to survive the dangers of Zephras. You also might end up with your throat slit in a ditch. Ultimately that's entirely up to you.

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps.
Winds guide you, <name>.

Can you hear it? The whispers of the winds? Doubtful, considering that the spirits stopped speaking with us when they left us those years ago. 

Those among us who would seek audience with the spirits of the four winds once more hone our understanding of the elements and the natural world, dearly hoping to reestablish the dialogue that was so abruptly ended. 

Would you walk this path and master the elements?

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps and I will train you.

Checked in with Illaya then? Great. Lots of tension between the High Order and the Windshapers these days, but they keep things civil here in Shen'dar. Everyone here is well aware that we've got bigger problems than their quibbles.

Now that that's done, you look like someone who might be looking for something to do with their hands and I've got a bandit problem that I was hoping you could help me with.

With the bandits dispersed, that is one less problem for us to deal with. Though I confess that now I worry that any bandits who survived may turn next to the cult for protection, further bolstering their increasingly alarming numbers.

Still though, we'll take the victories where we can get them.
What did you learn?

Lorthuna herself was there? She's the leader of the whole damned cult!

If they are making a move on Shen'dar Village and the western watchtower, we've got to be ready. What is strange is... why the watchtower?

The Village I can understand, but the tower? It doesn't have much strategic significance, other than as a minor lookout post.

Regardless, we will be prepared for them. They'll find that highlanders aren't as easy to catch flat footed as they might think.

What is this? A new acolyte seeking to serve the windlord sent by sister Sania? Truly we are blessed by the touch of the four winds this day!

We welcome all who seek to bask in the blessings of Al'Akir.
So you've come for training, then?

You are about to embark upon a dangerous journey. Our world is changing and it will need those who have the will to lead and protect others if our people hope to survive. As you grow in power you will need guidance. Come to me--I will do what I can to train you as you progress.

Good luck, <name>, may the winds guide you.
It feels good to turn the tables on these zealots.

Thank the winds you've returned!

Sania Silverstream snuck out of town just before you returned, no doubt fleeing at the sight of our people arming themselves.

You've done an incredible thing for the people of Shen'dar Village and we owe you a debt of gratitude. If the cult returns to the highlands, they will find that Shen'dar is not such an easy target.

Winds guide you, <name>.
There's a lot of hungry and desperate skyborne here who need these supplies.

This is great! We've been barely squeaking by without our regular supply deliveries. I'll work with the constable to ensure that these supplies get redistributed to the townsfolk who are in most dire need.
No matter how much things change here on Zephras and how uncertain things get, I always say that a pipe full of dried peacebloom and nice full belly is a comfort that can't be beat!

These eggs aren't easy to get but wind save me, they are DELICIOUS fried up in a bit of ursera tallow.

If you've got a bit of time to spare and you enjoy cooking, I can teach you a few tips and tricks I've picked up. Say the word and I'd be happy to train you.
A letter from Aonda. What's that crafty highlander been up to?

<Valennia's expression darkens as she reads the letter.>

Aonda trusted you to deliver this and she speaks highly enough of you in this letter, so I'll try to trust you too. Before we speak further, I need to consult with the few peacekeepers we have left here and formulate a plan in case the cult strikes here next. Enjoy your stay in Valanaar for now.

If you are looking to keep yourself busy, there are plenty of townsfolk that can likely use the help of a strong young adventurer like yourself.
The world is changing and the path forward will be difficult. We have but one chance to save ourselves.

I think you now understand how important the mission of the Windshapers is. Every soul who commands the skysight is of vital importance if we hope to establish dialogue with the spirits of the winds once again.

Between threats from within such as the Al'Aketh, and the uncertainty of our safety here in Skywall, it is our responsibility as Windshapers to use our gifts to save our home and ensure that the Shen'dorei can survive these trying times.
Our land is going through changes, but there may yet be some good to come of this.

Like a muscle, your skysight must be exercised if you hope to grow stronger in the gift. Leveraging your skysight to bridge the distance between the mortal and the spiritual may prove invaluable to you in your adventures.

You'd do well to remember what you've learned here today. Our ability to use our gifts to hear what the elements tell us could be the key to our survival.
Tensions between the Windshapers and High Order are high right now, but we couldn't hope to carry out this plan without both groups on board.
You are still alive? Thank the winds for small miracles, I suppose.
<This man is clearly dead, killed by the assassins that you fought outside the house. As you kneel down to inspect the body you notice the glinting reflection of something shiny...>
You are back? And... alone?

The turncoat was already dead when you arrived, you say? This is unfortunate news.

<You hand over the crystal you found on the dead cultist's body.>

Interesting...

Belguilos is dead? Four winds bless you, <class>. 

We might just make it out of this alive after all.

I sent a few of our healers to ensure that Valennia and her remaining forces made it back in one piece. She should be resting in the High Elder's residence now.

Muln has already departed back to Azeroth, but he and I spoke of what is next for the Windshapers and our mission to Azeroth. Unfortunately, the island is more vulnerable than ever now and we need a plan to protect Zephras from what is to come.
What? Alvarion is alive?

<Aamelia listens while you explain what became of Alvarion.>

At least I know he's going to be safe in Valanaar.

Stranger, I hate to tell you this but I think my idiot husband likely just sent you here to die for nothing. If you have any sense at all, you should leave now. This isn't your fight.

These bandits are more likely to double cross and steal from each other than they are to steal from normal folks. I bet if Ferauu knew some of his people went rogue and came here early to tamper with the harvest, he'd kill them himself.
I watched you take down those bandits from the window. Not bad.
Flutterflies are normally docile and calm, but rub them the wrong way and sometimes they'll surprise you.

This stuff can be a bit messy and it tends to get everywhere. You'll probably be shaking this out of your trousers for weeks, unfortunately. I do appreciate it, though. I've had this on my to-do list for weeks, but getting too far from the house when it's just me on my own with bandits lurking everywhere is a big risk.

Don't bother asking me what I use this stuff for. Things. Stuff and things. Don't worry about it.
I don't think I've had real meat for dinner in... well, too long.
These are big tenderloins! You must have taken down some real monsters out there.

If you manage to bring me enough bandit masks, maybe I'll stitch a blanket out of them and give it to Ferauu.

<Aamelia laughs loudly.>

When I said the bloodier the better, you really listened. Good. It lets me know you made it hurt.

On a serious note, thank you for what you've done so far. I've been floating aimlessly around this farm for weeks as if I was just waiting for the end to come. I think I'm starting to have hope again.

Ferauu and his thugs are due any time now. All that's left is to go out and face them. What do you say, will you see this through to the end with me?
There's not enough stormapples in skywall to repay you for this.
I... can't believe it's over. I need to stop and calm myself before my heart leaps right out of my chest.

The construct? It's been wandering around the fields for decades. Since the wind elementals left us, I think. Alvarion suspected that it used to haul harvests to market, or maybe tend to livestock back before this was an orchard. That could have been a thousand years ago though.

In the old days, the Windshapers used to maintain these constructs. We've talked about petitioning them to come and take a look at it, but it's never been a pressing concern to us. Mostly we just ignore it these days.

Hello and welcome. Rathiril sent me a magical missive about you and he mentioned you had some promise.

With you standing before me now, I can see why he suggested you seek me out. You have a vibrant arcane aura about you. Few enough of us anymore have the aptitude, let alone the will, to do what is needed to save our home. Do you have the boldness and strength needed to aid The High Order?

I suppose we will see.

Elder Amberwind sent me a message about you and your exploits in Shen'dar Village. You are most welcome here, friend.

You have a strong aura, and you clearly have a resonance with the spirits. Fewer and fewer of us have the skysight of late, and Zephras needs those with the gift if we are to survive these trying times. I am glad you have found your way to me.

I look forward to further making your acquaintance.
A letter from Aonda. What's that crafty highlander been up to?

<Valennia's expression darkens as she reads the letter.>

Aonda trusted you to deliver this and she speaks highly enough of you in this letter, so I'll try to trust you too. Before we speak further, I need to consult with the few peacekeepers I have left here and formulate a plan in case the cult strikes here next. Enjoy your stay in Valanaar for now.

If you are looking to keep yourself busy, there are plenty of townsfolk that can likely use the help of a strong young adventurer like yourself.

<Alvarion's eyes tear up as you finish retelling the story of what happened at the orchard.>

I don't know how to thank you, friend. I came to Valanaar looking for hope. A vain hope, I was almost certain. But instead I found a hero. A real hero, like the stories from before we came to Skywall. 

I'll never forget what you did for us, <name>. You'll always be welcome at the Windfield home.
What can I do for ya, <race>?

Finally, somebody killed that thing! Do you know how hard it is to get a crew in the water when everyone in town's crying "Shark!" all the time?

I might just put that monster's fin into a soup for dinner tonight, just to have the last laugh.

So now you see? There is a world of knowledge and untapped potential outside of Skywall. This will never stop being our home, but I've come to believe that the path to our salvation lies below. We must travel to Azeroth and gain the power and means to save Zephras Isle. This is the way.

Will you have the courage to join us when the time comes?

So do you now see? Rediscovering the ancient magic of our forebears is the key to unlocking the secrets of Zephras Isle and securing our future, but in order to save our home, we must rediscover what we've lost these past millennia.

Azeroth is the key. The Kirin Tor will show us the way.

While we make ready to leave, you should check in with the other members of the High Order here in Valanaar. Most of them have tasks that they could use help from one such as yourself to see completed.

<The satchel lying before you has a few specks of what appears to be dried blood on the flap. Studying the stain you also notice that the flap also has a name embroidered onto it. It reads "Fillion Flamebreeze".>

The High Order does not make it a habit to employ themselves as simple trappers and game wardens, but when performing a service such as this can lead to scholarly gain, we are happy to engage in acts of community service.

That is quite the haul of talons you've brought me. I cannot wait to dig into this!

Thank you for your service to the High Order, <class>.
Need something blown up?
Show me those explosives, <name>!
This is a great start! Now to tie it all together... and add a little extra zing...
Hmm... Looking for something specific, are you?
Did you get a remote detonator? A normal one simply won't do!
Great--that's exactly what we need!
Were your efforts in Stormwind fruitful?
I'm glad you've returned, <name>.
So you found the forge, and planted the bomb... only one thing remains to be done.
I don't know what to say, <name>. To think that Stormwind would put their military ambitions over the livelihood of their people...

I don't agree with the Windshapers often, but they were right to dismiss the idea of trying to engage peacefully with the Al'Aketh. My attempt to take the high road cost a dear friend his life and is a mistake I will have to live with for the rest of my days.

The High Order prides ourselves in our pragmatism and logic, and logic dictates that the avoidance of conflict and loss of life is the most prudent option in most situations.

<Elaadrin's eyes begin to glow and crackle with arcane energy.>

...however, the cult mistook our prudence for weakness and they are not nearly ready to pay the cost of that error.

It's often difficult for me to establish a distinction between the Windshapers and the Al'Aketh, save that one is more overtly violent than the other. Equally slavish to their misplaced beliefs, they are both equally dangerous if left to their own devices.

They see our desire to better understand this realm and its magic as a desecration of their traditions. Their small-mindedness is why our mission is so important. If not us, who will have the courage to save Zephras?

It would not have been my preference to spill Windshaper blood but the blame for this pointless conflict rests solely on their shoulders. We sought to peacefully gather information, and they responded with violence.

Unfortunately, word has spread and the Windshapers are already calling it a 'massacre'. They wouldn't dare to retaliate here in Valanaar, but they will certainly not forget.

<name>, you have been of tremendous aid to the High Order. Thank you.

Th... thank you, stranger. I was returning from an assignment at the Overlook Standing Stones when I was suddenly ambushed and attacked by Windshapers. They forced me over to the mouth of the cave and left me there, barely conscious and bleeding. The last thing I remember before blacking out is a massive winged beast emerging from the cave and scooping me up.

I think it's safe to say that if you hadn't come along, I'd have been dinner for that beast and its younglings.
Those shrieklings are too dangerous to be left to nest this close to Valanaar. However... they are the least of our troubles.
Thank you again, <name>.

I am sorry to hear about Belathaan. He was actually my cousin and he was a good mage and servant of Zephras. We will avenge him.

You seem eager to lend aid immediately. Come, let's speak further on the current situation.
You seem eager to lend aid immediately. Come, let's speak further on the current situation.

<Valennia looks visibly relieved as you tell her about the status of the eastern watchtower.>

Thank the winds.
I have a small matter that requires just the kind of assistance that an adventurer like yourself can provide.
It's a mess out there, <name>! Did you collect the parts I need?
Thanks a bunch! I'll get to work on an escape plan. In the meantime, take this!
What's this?
How's the project coming, <name>?

Here it is, <name>! Should work great. Go give it a try!

...Me? No, I'll stay here. It's starting to feel like home, anyway.
We fought hard to get this far but it isn't over yet.

Greetings child, my name is Sania Silverstream and I am a junior priestess in the Order of the Al'Aketh. Do you wish to learn more of our sovereign, the Windlord Al'Akir?

There is always room at the Windlord's table for the righteous and the repentant.
We are as ready as we'll ever be.

It gladdens me to hear that we have High Elder Shadowsong's blessing for our expedition. Now that the cult has been defeated and preparations have been made, I think it's finally time.

Ansirem has worked diligently to help us get stable skycutter transport going between the city of Dalaran and Zephras Isle. We've done as much testing as we can, and the time has come for our vanguard to depart.

I'm pleased to hear that we have High Elder Shadowsong's blessing for our expedition. Now that the cult has been defeated and preparations have been made, I think it's finally time.

Muln has worked diligently to help us get stable skycutter transport going between Zephras Isle and a place called Mulgore, where the Earthen Ring make their home. We've been doing test voyages and some of our people are already waiting on the other side.
So that's the story...

...that's about all I have to say about it. I was--um--somewhere else before I was here. Now I'm here and I have my friends, and my things. T-things I built, I mean. That's about all I need. I think that's all I need, anyway.

I have to say though, it is nice to talk to someone who will talk back. The forest spirits try, but they just end up singing at me. That's nice in its own way, but not exactly s-stimulating conversation.
Mmm, I think you are going to like what I can cook up with these acorns!

Thank you, stranger! You'll find that these are delicious once roasted! 

Please excuse me, it won't take me long to whip this up.
I will not rest until my fangs have gone through the throat of every single cultist on this isle.

Excellent work. Only good things can happen by eliminating the cult. Hopefully this sends a message that the Nightclaw are not to be trifled with and that our resentments run deep.

I suspect you have your work cut out for yourself, taking on the cult. If you gather more ears bring them here.
We can only hope that those poor spirits are able to find peace after being freed from this place.
Thank you, stranger.

Windsong Crawler meat is common enough here but it was something of a delicacy on the islands of Anvilas and Siroccas. Was a time, back when the skystreams were open that the locals would mob me for the stuff when I'd make the trip to Shen'dramar or New Eldre'naar.

Not been able to visit those places in... well... a long time.

Winds bless me this meat looks fantastic! 

Thank you so much, <class>.
I'll need the creature's head as proof of the deed.

If we didn't have enough on our plates between the cult and the highlands bandits, we don't need a giant vuldren terrorizing our citizens as well. You've done a great thing here today. As promised, here is your reward.

These sneakthieves have likely been breaking into our supplies for months. I tried to convince Aonda to put a raid together to clear out that bandit cave for good, but she didn't want to pull the few peacekeepers we have away from the village. 

With the cultists at Falaath Village to the south growing in numbers, I suppose I can't fault her for that.
Thanks <class>. This should help us get by for now. If we can't get the supply routes squared away soon though, a few stolen windstones will be the least of our worries.
We are holding them off for now, but they have greater numbers and our fighters are starting to get tired. We need to do something to break the stalemate, and do it fast.
<Vayn nods at you.>
As promised, here is your reward.

<Riaani's face is buried under the heaving armor plates of the construct, attempting to work on the mechanisms underneath. He does not notice your presence at all.>

Storms curse where is the core?! Who thought it would be a good idea to remove the Gyrozephyr as well? It's a miracle this construct's winds haven't dissipated entirely by now!
Shadowgale Forest is a dangerous place. Some even say its haunted. I'm quite sure that I don't believe that, but I do know that its not for the faint hearted, or the unprepared.

Handling these essences fills me with a sense of... deep disquiet. I can almost feel a malevolent, regretful aura emanating from them. It's enough to make me faint.

<Endaria shudders slightly.>

I do not look forward to studying these further.

I can't imagine why anyone would want to steal these components from this construct. Other than the gyrozephyr these components have almost no practical application. Even the gyro would be nigh-useless outside of its intended purpose.

Thank you for scavenging these materials. I imagine that some of this wasn't terribly easy to get. 

With these parts I can get the construct up and running again. From there we can just hope that its memory is intact and it can tell us who took its components.

Very interesting, so it was the High Order that was responsible for the construct breaking down?

I know Belathaan. He's Valennia Stormfist's cousin and his mother was actually a Windshaper. It's disappointing that he was involved in this.

I need to reflect on this for a moment.
The Al'Aketh have engaged in their bloody zealotry for far too long. This is only the start of the reckoning they face.

<Ayessa looks shaken and distant as you hand her the windstone charms.>

Don't mind me, <name>. Today has merely been... a trying day. Thank you for your service to the windshapers thus far.

Wait--what?! Belathaan... is dead? 

<Ayessa listens as you give your account of what occurred.> 

The High Order was meeting with the Al'Aketh to discuss peace? There is no peace with the cult, they are murderous zealots. What was Elaadrin thinking sending Belathaan to treat with them alone?

Pay this no mind, <name>. You are not at fault for this. The arrogance of the High Order is to blame, yet again. You were merely in the right place at the wrong time.
Ah, you must be <name>? It is heartening to see young mages eager to learn our ways and history. Come, I will explain the next steps to crafting your spell focus.

Every year that passes in Zephras sees fewer and fewer of those who are gifted with a talent for magic. 

I am glad to see young mages such as yourself participate in our oldest traditions to help keep our history and culture alive and well.

Thank you, <name>. I can indeed feel the elemental energies in this bough waiting to be harnessed by those that have the gift to do so. This will make an excellent spell focus.

Did this branch sing to you, perhaps? It has often been the case that the branch picks the <class>, and not the other way around.

I sent a few of our remaining mages to ensure that Valennia and her forces were able to escape as well. She should be resting at High Elder Shadowsong's residence now.

Ansirem had to return to Azeroth, but he and I discussed the next steps for the High Order before he departed. We survived the day, but Zephras is dangerously vulnerable now and we must make plans for what is to come.

<Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Ayessa's plan to leave Zephras Isle.>

I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet and on the timeline of elemental gods, it could be years... decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.

There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.

<The body here is somewhat fresh, clearly only recently having been killed. Judging by the burns and scorch marks on this peacekeeper's skin, its clear that they were killed by the cult's storm-wielding spellcasters.>
What news from the western watch?

So they are all dead, then. Storms curse on these cult bastards!

While you managed to take out the priest and stop the cultists at the tower, I confess that I'm now doubly concerned about whatever it was you said that they were doing to the pylon. The fact that there was such a massive cache of windstones there with them tells me that they needed enormous energy for it.

I have to wonder, what's the end goal here? Violating the pylon, attacking the village? To what end?
(PH) Thanks!
What is that you have for me? Oh... oh no.

I... am very sorry to hear that my nephew is dead. I thank you kindly for recovering this, and bringing it to me.

It's not common that such capable young shen'dorei come down from the highlands. If you need work, please speak with Valennia Stormfist, the captain of the peacekeepers here in Valanaar. These days we need all the help we can get.
I'm sure there are more of these critters around Valanaar, but every enchanted skyhopper we stomp out makes the city just a tiny bit safer.
What beautiful things did you bring me?

It might seem a bit of a vain triviality, gathering feathers for our hair. However, even in times like these, one needs to embrace the small joys as much as possible. 

If one thing I create brings someone joy, then I will consider that to be a good day. Thank you for bringing me these and helping me bring some joy to Zephras.
<Valennia looks gravely wounded.>

Ah, you are back.

I hope your adventures have given you a sense of the scale and wonder of our world. I know it must seem overwhelming to you, but if you are to help your people, you must be prepared for whatever may come your way while you are on Azeroth.

While you wait for your order to establish itself in Dalaran, I suggest you turn your attention to the lands around Stormwind. Westfall in particular can always use more strong adventurers to lend them aid, if you are willing.
<Seena nods curtly at you.>

You have done what I could not and restored my family honor. For this, I will bestow a gift that few on Zephras are worthy to receive. I will teach out the secrets of the Skybreaker Defense.

Also, you will need a shield to put what I have to teach you into practice. Please, take this one. I have little use for it now that the Skybreaker Bulwark has been returned to me.

Banu'Adoraah, friend.
So, you wish to embrace the way of the claw, child? Very well. Let us speak.
I am most glad that you came. Come, let us begin.
You will learn, <name>, and one day you will be a great <class>.

Excellent, <name>! You are quite a fast learner. Now that you know the basics, I can teach you how to forge a lasting bond with an animal companion.

Go with this knowledge and thrive. Be the <class> that Zephras Isle needs you to be.

A fledgling <class>, I see. Yes, I can bestow you with the skills you need to train and guide your pet. Not only will you be able to teach your pet new abilities, you will now be able to feed your pet, as well as revive it, should it fall in battle.

Remember, <name>, always respect the balance and live in awe of nature around you. Now, go forth. We shall speak again, at a later date.

<Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Elaadrin's plan to leave Zephras Isle.>

I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet, and on the timeline of elemental demigods, it could be years... decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.

There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.

Patience, lad, is the earth's finest virtue. It's seen mountains crumble and rivers carve valleys--slow and stubborn, like a true <race>. The earth calls to ye now, for trouble brews on the horizon. Return successful, and ye'll be one step closer to bein' whole.

Others may envy yer wisdom, but that's their burden to bear.

Well done, lad. Ye've proven yerself ready. Earth's the bedrock of all things. It'll shield ye, but only if ye show it proper respect. Even stone can shift if slighted. Learn its ways, and ye'll grow wiser than most. Never forget the secrets it shares. 

I'll craft ye a sapta now--accept it, and ye'll walk the true path.

Ahh, ye've returned. If ye have the stone, it means the mountain's chosen ye true. I'll give ye the totem it promised. But if ye've come empty-handed, off with ye! The path ain't for those who forget their way.

Well done! Know this--totems ain't just a mark of yer place among shamans. They're tools, a focus for spells tied to stone, soil, and other elements. As ye grow wiser, more o' the mountain's power will open to ye. The trainers will know when yer ready for more. But for now, take this totem, and let the ground speak through ye.

Direct conflict with our shen'dorei brothers and sisters only weakens us as a people, but decisive action must at times be taken to prevent greater tragedy.

The mages of the High Order have zero regard for the consequences of their magical meddling. The forces that bind our island are fragile and vulnerable and all it could take is one thoughtless action to destroy our home.

My gift is simple, and mundane. I cannot peer between worlds such as those with the skysight, nor can I draw upon the magic of the ley lines beneath Zephras like others can. But a gift it remains and I am grateful to have it.

Appreciation of what you have is the key to happiness. Yearning for what you may have, or what you have lost, only leads to despair.
You... you are a <class>? Please, do not hurt me. I-I know I'm not supposed to be panhandling. I have no quarrel with you or your order. Leave me be, I beg you!
I hope that this is no imposition upon you, goodly <class>.
This is very kind of you, <class>. Very kind indeed.

You have done well, <name>. It was a small thing, but even small acts of service such as this may help strengthen our connection to the light.

The Dark Lady and many in her service mistrust us. Some even conspire against us, but we will visit their skepticism and fear with courage and righteousness. We will show them that we are members of the Forsaken and we are willing to do our part, be it large or small, to help our people prosper once again.

Take this symbol, you will need it for what comes next.

So you'll help me, then? Good, good. I'll admit I'm not proud of resorting to... well, resorting to asking paladins for aid. The priests waved me away and you might be my friend's only chance.

Please, help me.

I'm... back? And saved by a <class> no less? I see you carry a Symbol of Life. I've not seen one of those since... well, since before the war when Lordaeron was a very different place. I can only assume you are here to help. Billmuth and I were sent here to scout out the scarlet activity here, and we found out that they are planning some kind of attack.

If you would be willing to help more, there may yet be more that you can do to help the Forsaken.
What news of Deathguard Falgan?

Thank you for saving my friend, <name>. I will take these plans back to my commander and we will give those crusaders a welcoming they won't forget.

I know that many among our people mistrust you paladins, but it's clear to me that you are Forsaken through and through. I won't forget this, and I'll make sure others know of what you did here today.

The Symbol of Life is only able to be used by a <class> who is ready to make use of one of the light's greatest blessings. I'm proud to count you among us, and I now bestow upon you the gift of redemption. With this you will be able to resurrect your fallen companions. Use this new boon wisely.

You have done well for both the Forsaken as well as the paladins of Bandarion Keep. Any steps we can take to win the hearts and minds of our fellow Forsaken is well worth the effort. Go with the light, <name>.

Thank goodness our message got to Lotheluum. Wait, where are the rest of the reinforcements? Surely it is not just you they sent?

<Elegael pales as you relay your conversation with Lotheluum.>

So the message did not get through. We are in dire straights indeed then.

It seems we must handle this on our own. Time is of the essence.
Have you found the Lady's Tear?

<Elegael takes the sticky mound of moss from you with a weak smile.>

Thank you, <name>, you have done well. This is exactly what we need.
It deeply saddens me to ask you to kill the young shrieklings, but with the rise in their aggression it is for the best. We can only handle so many emergencies at a time.
Thank you for these. I will be sure to use every feather so their sacrifice will not be in vain.
I will make the cult pay for every drop of druid blood they have spilled this day.

<Elegael looks down at the collection of bloodied heirlooms with distress.>

So many young lives with so much potential now gone forever. Thank you for returning these, <class>.

I will hold onto them for safe keeping until I am able to take them to the High Elder. There they can go back into the collection and await the next and perhaps more worthy generation to come of age.
Are our brethren's lives truly worth so little to you, Haalien?

<Elegael grimaces at the severed head, but nods curtly.>

Thank you, <name>. No matter how much rage I have within me, it would have been difficult to strike down my own cousin.

Do not mourn for him. His ignorance and malice has killed many innocents this day.
<class>! You have returned. Were you able to reach my brothers and sisters? Did you find Jorel?

<Elegael's face pales as you relay the fate of Jorel and the condition of the rest of the druids.>

No... no! This is far worse than I had--

<Elegael chokes back a sob and grits her teeth, letting out a pained snarl.>

They will pay. They will ALL pay. Anyone who allies with the Al'Aketh will feel my wrath! This I swear.

They were here for the pylon? But to what end? We were not the original reason for their attack?

<Elegael trails off shaking with rage as she reads.>

They murdered my people because we were an inconvenience! I shall tear apart every cultist with my fangs! I will make sure none leave this place with their lives.

Go, swiftly! If the orders truly originated in Valanaar, it means it is likely a traitor hiding there. Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar and tell him what has transpired.

<Lotheluum wears a look of genuine terror as you recount the events from the druid den.>

I--I'm sorry, <name>. I need just a moment. There are no words I possess that can describe the loss.

This is grave news indeed. If this missive is not fabricated, then we indeed have at best an accomplice and at worst a traitor here in Valanaar. I will take this to the High Elder immediately! I will not let my fellows' sacrifice be in vain.

The Al'aketh Cultists ambushed us with little to no warning. Many inside my den lay wounded or dying. I had attempted to send a message to Valanaar but it appears my efforts were in vain.

Please, if you have come here I beg for your help. I don't know how much longer my fellows will be able to survive this onslaught.
That turncoat risked everything to escape the cult and bring us this crystal...

We could try and send peacekeepers to directly engage the cult forces, but we would not fare well against them in open battle.

We are going to need a different approach.

The agony I feel over her loss is immeasurable, but it is what is necessary for the balance. You have demonstrated a resolve to persevere, even when a terrible price is asked.

You have done well, <class>. I shall grant you the blessing to take on the shape of my kin. Be a beacon for those that lack the strength to persevere and a defender of those in need.

Go now, and embrace the way of the claw, child.
You will learn, <name>, and one day you will be a great <class>.
Excellent, <name>! You are quite a fast learner.

A fledgling <class>, I see. Yes, I can bestow you with the skills you need to train and guide your pet. Not only will you be able to teach your pet new abilities, you will now be able to feed your pet, as well as revive it, should it fall in battle.

Remember, <name>, always respect the balance and live in awe of nature around you. Now, go forth. We shall speak again, at a later date.
With learning, <name>, comes mastery.
Well done, <name>! You're quite in tune with the beast.
Go forth, <name>, and tame the burliest of Elwynn beasts.
The brawn of the forest. Brave work, <name>!
So many of us left with nothing more than the clothes on our backs. Any belongings you might recover would be cherished.
Thank you, <class>, you have done a great kindness to us refugees this day. I will make sure to return these to their owners. At least it gives us a place to start over from.

records.currentEnglish: Have you any news of Resaan? Please, <class>, the wait is hard to endure after everything that has happened.

<Ealaane's eyes well with tears.>

Oh, Resaan my love. What will become of us now? There was so much... it feels as if our lives together had just started.

Thank you, <class>. The world is cruel to take both my home and my love from me. At least his heirloom will give me some closure.

Ah, you've made it. Wonderful. It's going to take us some time to get ourselves established here, so you may want to take some time to explore the city. Be warned however, try not to venture too far from the safety of the city proper.  

As idyllic as this new land appears, it can be extremely dangerous to wander outside of Dalaran without appropriate preparation and experience.

records.currentEnglish:
Well met, <class>. I am Bolvar Fordragon, regent to the throne of Stormwind.

A Kirin Tor messenger told me to expect to receive members of the High Order, and here you stand. It's been some time since a high elf has stood in this throne room, but I am glad to accept you now as a guest.

On behalf of the King, I welcome you to Stormwind and give you leave to travel freely through alliance lands. Welcome to Azeroth, Skyborne.
You will learn, <name>, and one day you will be a great <class>.
Well tamed, <name>! You are becoming adept already.
You will learn, <name>, and one day you will be a great <class>.
You're back already! Impressive speed, <name>!
You look chilly, <class>. How goes the hunt?
These pelts will make excellent saddles. You've done the Alliance proud, <class>!
I trust you did not get lost?

You say there is evil in Shadowvale? I admit, I am not surprised. The forest folk were an odd lot, and they did not care for visitors. Some believe the Whispering Forest itself is cursed, and the elixir distilled from its roots carries that same curse...

...but enough of superstition and rumors, <name>. Thank you for the elixirs. Here, take this as payment.
Do you have something for me, <class>?

What an interesting specimen. From underneath the Whispering Forest, you say? It's no secret that foul place is touched by the void.

I welcome the opportunity to explore the mysteries of shadow, <class>. Allow me to offer you payment for what you've found.

More adventurers from Zephras, I see. Wonderful. The winds surely favor us! It's going to take us some time to get ourselves established here, so you may want to take some time to explore this new land.

Azeroth is an exciting new world, but it's also a dangerous world. You'd do well to prepare yourself for this new adventure by familiarizing yourself with the lands nearby.

Lok-tar, <class>. I am Thrall, Warchief of the Horde.

An Earthen Ring messenger told me to expect members of the Windshapers, and here you are. I'd not have expected to see a high elf standing before me here in Orgrimmar, but the Horde will welcome you as our guest all the same.

You have my blessing to travel through Horde lands. Go with honor, Windshaper.
How goes the hunt?

Yes, these look like they will do nicely. I have an arrangement with a local tanner to deliver these raw hides in exchange for various finished leather goods that I use as part of my trade. 

I've never come up short on my end of the arrangement, and even with my injury I do not intend to start now.
Greetings, <class>. What brings you up to my property today?
Vrang sent you then? Very well. I appreciate you delivering these hides to me. It's unfortunate that Vrang couldn't make the journey himself. There is a matter I wish to speak with him about.
<Vrang grunts at you as you approach.>
Thank you for your aid, <class>. I was starting to wonder if I'd have to go to bed hungry tonight because this cursed wound on my leg.

Well, looks like we are all alive. I... knew that someday that would catch up to me. I'm in your debt for your help here today.

Please, take this. It's not much, but it's the least I can do.

Safe travels, <class>.

The remnants of Daelin Proudmoore's fleet who still fly his banner are just as rotten and barbaric as the admiral himself was before he died.

I don't know why they are so far from Tiragarde, but it can't be good.
So they are looking for a deserter... Well, it seems that the past has finally caught up to me.
I have only memories now, but I will build a tribute to Olgra so that they never fade.

I will place these adornments with Olgra's memorial, so that I never forget her. My blood will always run hot with revenge from this day until my last day. Each swing of my blade and enemy felled will be in her name.

You have done me... done us... a great honor. 

Lok-tar, <name>.
Why are you addressing me, <class>?

I don't doubt Danitha's sincerity and desire to earn a place for your kind amongst the Forsaken. However, I suspect that this isn't the last time we'll see one of your brothers and sisters go mad and turn the light against their own people.

There may come a time when I decide that tolerating your misbegotten order is no longer in the best interests of the Forsaken. I suggest you continue to serve your people diligently.

We will be watching.
<The smoke from the incense rises toward the sky.>
<As you empty the incense into the fire, the scent wafts around you, leaving you with just the empty pouch and a subtle sense of fulfillment.>

Ever since the barrier went down around Dalaran, the Kirin Tor have maintained a death grip on the roads. They're paranoid about something, that much is certain.

For now, however, the why is irrelevant.
Having the skills needed to survive the outdoors are critical. A well-rested and well-prepared adventurer has a much higher chance of surviving this lifestyle.
So now that we've learned the basics, why don't you go and learn a tradeskill. They will also teach you the know-how to create a proper camp fixture suitable to your new profession.
Have you found the big wolf?
Taking the life of such a beautiful creature is a sad event, but it was necessary for the safety of our people. I will make certain that the pelt does not go to waste. Thank you.
Having the skills needed to survive the outdoors are critical. A well-rested and well-prepared adventurer has a much higher chance of surviving this lifestyle.

So now that we've learned the basics, why don't you go and learn a tradeskill from the trainers in the village nearby. They will also teach you how to create a camp fixture suitable to your new profession.
A good campfire is the foundation to any good camp.

With this, you'll be able to set up a camp anywhere out in the wilderness. What you've learned is just the basics, so you won't be able to place too many furnishings around it.

Raise your cooking skill and you might just be able to learn to make even bigger fires.

You can also learn the basics of furnishing your campsites from other tradeskill trainers if you're savvy in their skills.

I appreciate the lookin' out, <class>. That marshal's just a worrywart.

Hey, you've got the look of an adventurer yourself. How would you like to learn about camping?
A good campfire is the foundation to any good camp.

With this, you'll be able to set up a camp anywhere out in the wilderness. What you've learned is just the basics, so you won't be able to place too many furnishings around it.

Raise your cooking skill and you might just be able to learn to make even bigger fires.

You can also learn the basics of furnishing your campsites from other tradeskill trainers if you're savvy in their skills.

I'm not affiliated with the Scarlet Crusade, if you couldn't tell. I'm just an adventurer stopping by before my next venture into the wilderness.

Hey, you've got the look of an adventurer yourself. How would you like to learn about camping?
A good campfire is the foundation to any good camp.

With this, you'll be able to set up a camp anywhere out in the wilderness. What you've learned is just the basics, so you won't be able to place too many furnishings around it.

Raise your cooking skill and you might just be able to learn to make even bigger fires.

You can also learn the basics of furnishing your campsites from other tradeskill trainers if you're savvy in their skills.
The peons have been scared to travel south for some time, <name>. Now that you've cleared the path a bit, we can get them back to work.
Have you done what I asked?
These warriors will always be remembered, <name>. You have made sure of that.
Did you find the fruits?
I'll use these to prepare something tasty, and save the seeds for planting. Someday we'll have prickly pears growing all around Orgrimmar!
What do you have for me, <name>?
Fine work. A shame about the slain trolls, but with the binding spells removed, their spirits can rest.
Yes?
These spines are tougher than I expected, <name>! Crafting with them may not be as easy as I thought... but I'll keep working on it!
Yes?
Your work helps Orgrimmar grow. Know that as you walk the city's paths.
Something need doing?
My pack! When I dropped it to run from that huge spider, I thought I'd never see it again. You really are a hero!
Yes?
What a trophy, <class>! That must have been some fight!
Stay low and try not to be seen, <class>. These cultists are not to be trifled with.

I plan to stay here for a time and speak with more of my friends, but I will return to Light's Hope Chapel in Eastern Plaguelands soon enough. Should you ever find yourself out that way, please do say hello. We could always use more help from able-bodied adventurers.
Thank you for your aid, <class>. If we do not wish to see Lordaeron's history repeat itself, we've got to be vigilant when threats like this spring up.
I'd advise you not come into too much physical contact with those crystals. Even shattered and spent, the lingering magic in these necrotic crystals is highly dangerous.

Thank you. This should slow the efforts of the Scourge in this area. I suspect the denizens of Tirisfal will be pulling these crystals out of the ground for years, but removing the most conspicuous of them can only help.

This place is full of memories for me. This place was once held by the Argent Dawn. It was from here that we prepared for many battles and skirmishes against the Scourge during their most recent push into Tirisfal Glades.

When we withdrew to the Plaguelands I feared it would fall into disrepair. My fear was well-founded, but I am glad that Danitha and her paladins have taken over stewardship of it now.

She even named the keep after... a mutual friend.

The Bloodtalon are known for their cunning and swiftness, and make fine companions when raised from egg to adult.

Unfortunately adult raptors are very difficult to train, and I have tried to capture the Matriarch on more than one occasion. But she had become too dangerous of late.

Still I hope to preserve her legacy by raising her children as companions here in Sen'Jin.
Thank you, <name>. I am happy we will be able to preserve her bloodline and raise them to be our allies. You have done a great service for our tribe.
Have you found our loa idols, <name>? We must begin our rituals again soon.

You have done a great deed for our tribe today.

Unlike some tribes, our kinship with our loa is one of reverence and respect, and we owe them much.

I would not want the Darkspear to fall out of favor with them.

My, my. How I do love surprises, <name>.

This specimen will surely help further my studies.
Yes, <name>? What do you have there?
So you've brought the torch. Yes, young <class>, I can teach you to heed the call of fire. It will not be easy, but nothing that we do in this realm is ever easy.
The heart of a betrayer is a powerful reagent. The flames will eagerly accept such an offering and burn more intensely as it is consumed.

The Windshapers do not forget, and blood is always paid with blood. It pleases me that you were able to deliver this final, painful reminder of our creed to this traitor.

This heart will not be all that feeds the flames today, however. There is one other task that needs to done.
The spirit of Kuramaa is eternal, and it will manifest again when it is needed. It's mask is a source of great power, and will prove invaluable to the ritual we must complete.
We now have what we need. We will light the eternal flame and commune with the spirits of fire.
Not another word out of you until your pockets are jingling with metal!

Whooooa! Nice one, pal! You saved me from another one of Gagsprocket's unbearable lectures on the cost of metal. More importantly, I can jump right into building my next prototype.

Uhhh, I didn't have a reward planned... Do you like boxes?
You have done well to come this far. You do the Windshapers honor, <name>.

It is done. The Eternal Flame burns once again.

Your trial is now complete. I am pleased to present you with your Fire Totem. Use this icon of power well in your travels, <name>. 

Just remember, the power of the elemental plane serves those that respect it, and consumes those who do not. This is our way.

Throm'ka, <class>. Gorak told me I should be expecting you. It is good to see you in one piece!

Were you able to collect the training weapons I requested?
Thank you for returning these weapons, <name>. I will get to work repairing them for the next wave of recruits.

It is good to know that issue has been taken care of, but it saddens me that we could not find another way. Jai'vhanel had been somewhat of a guardian of this area for quite some time, and I am not sure what could have caused her descent into madness.

Regardless, thank you for your service today, <class>. The roads to Auberdine are safe for travel once again.

Ande'thoras-ethil.

Wait! Some drops yet remain in the phial! Perhaps that is why his incantation failed?

I apologize. As you have likely seen, we have many challenges to overcome.

Fandral is Arch Druid for now, and I ask you respect his station. But his doings pertain to druidism, and mine not only to Elune but indeed to lead our people as she wills.

Every drop of this water is blessed by our goddess. I thank you for saving it.
Good day, traveler. How can I assist?

You found the right place, and you're speaking with the right person! I can jot you down as one of our new associates. No paperwork necessary on your part, I can't be bothered with more of that.

All we ask of you is to assist in dealing with compromised deliveries you find during your travels. Doing so will earn you Merchant's Favor, which you can use to purchase goods and services right here. Here's a bit to get you settled in!

These pieces are all the proof I need that the curse has nothing to do with that blithering dolt.
Regrettably, that means his remedy is also worth nothing. It seems the search for a solution to the worgen curse continues.

It seems the Gilneans are not too keen on allowing anyone past their wall. That is fortunate, I suppose. It means there is likely no chance for the worgen curse to spread to their city.

Can you imagine the depravity if an entire kingdom were infected?
It'll be a hot day in Dun Morogh before I tell Paxton I lost his entire stockpile to a wendigo.

Yer a real lifesaver, <name>!

My husband would just laugh it off, but I couldn't bear tellin' him he has to spend another night on the lake. Maybe now we can enjoy a real feast.

May this help Executor Arren and so many others see our true nature. Much like in our past lives, we live to serve our people--to protect them with the gifts the Light provides us.

They will see in time that we are just as valuable to the Dark Lady's plans as any other.

Light be with you.
Have you wrested the amulets from the harpies' leaders?

<Arynia investigates the amulets.>

Do you see the foul green swirls within the gems? This is indeed fel moss corruption at work.

I have heard similar reports from Shadowglen and elsewhere in the boughs of this substance turning our very world against us.

I will inform my superiors of this at once.
As you inspect the fallen bark, a voice enters your mind. It is calm and soothing, cresting over you like a gentle breeze through the leaves.

<Tallonkai lowers his voice.>

Does Xethorr still walk freely?

I should have known this was being used to twist the spiders of this land.

I have heard whispers of this substance being the source of much of the corruption plaguing us. Though this is not the original, it is an older sample and may yield more information than what we have obtained so far.

Normally I would have you send this to Darnassus for further study. However, it is best we keep this quiet for the moment, or Dolanaar will never recover its reputation.

I trust you to do the same.
What is it you bring me, <class>?

Ah, this is most valuable knowledge. I thank you for your efforts.

<Morin looks through the notes.>

It seems our next move is clear.
Has the shredder been stopped, <name>?
All of Bloodhoof Village is in your debt this day. May the Earth Mother's grace stay with you always.

I am relieved that Longwalker Stormhoof is well. He is my most trusted scout, and his mission of the utmost importance.

Please, accept my thanks and my hospitality for risking your life to save his own. You have done a greater service to our people than you know.

I encourage you to explore our great city while you are here. It is a place of safety, and you will find many that may aid you on your own travels upon its bluffs.

Ish-ne-alo por-ah.

Ah, no wonder there is such joy running through the streams of Mulgore. You have done a great service today. The wells provide much for not only our people, but to the wildlife we depend on for food, clothing, and companionship.

It is my humble pleasure to honor Mull's request. Please, accept this token of my gratitude.
I wonder what they are after?

I'm glad you made it back. That group of Al'Aketh looked like stone cold killers. 

Thank you for your aid, I'll include your assistance in my report when I return to Valanaar.
What's that? You say that Leonid sent you? Oh boy, haven't seen that crusty old soldier since Naxxramas was raining hell down on our heads.

Thanks for delivering this, pal.

Wait... he said I'd tip you? I didn't agree to that! 

Fine. Take your pick of this junk in the lost and found. You'd be surprised how many of these Forsaken leave their stuff laying around after getting haircuts. There's a joke here about them being brainless, but I suspect in a lot of cases it might actually be true.
Through pain comes resolve.

Your training can now begin in earnest, <class>. I see great promise in you, but take care not to turn away from the light, even for a moment. Embrace the pain it will cause you. That pain is a crucible, and you will emerge from it stronger than you ever were in your previous life.
Elune's grace... I shall not die... alone...

The harpies have become afflicted by the same foulness showing up throughout the forest. I'm sure that is what ails Sentinel Eralya as well.

We must hurry. It won't be long before she succumbs to her injuries.

Heglan's body lies cold within the wreckage of the hut.
Whatever killed her doesn't seem to be human. There may be signs of what happened nearby.

Be proud of your kill today; not many can claim they survived a fight with a sea giant.

Thank Elune you were around to help Lynessa avoid a dark fate with the Gnarlpine. She's one of our best, and a personal friend.

Is the deed done?

You are covered in centaur blood. Remember this feeling. It is an honor unlike any other among our people.
I could hear the moment the last fell, and their thunderous stampede echoed no longer. Well done!
Today marks a great victory for our village, and a sense of security our young ones need now more than ever. You have my deepest thanks, young <class>.
This is most dire news indeed. We must inform Baine at once!

The Galak centaur dare show themselves in Mulgore?!
You have brought pride to your ancestors by driving them out. Perhaps that will remind them of the pain that awaits them should they do so again!
Please accept this gift in honor of this. May it serve you well as you venture out into the Earth Mother's kingdom, to the far reaches of this world.
What is it you bring me, <class>?

<Baine reads the report, his gaze darkening.>
This will not stand. Thank you for delivering it to me, <name>.

Ah, Pal'juh got herself in trouble again, did she?
Hopefully she learns her lesson about going alone this time. Thank you for helping her. She's a promising hunter, just tends to act more like a raptor than a tiger.

Are they dead?
I can hear their warbling from here--it'll be in my nightmares. Well, that should slow them down--although I have no doubt that they'll make up those numbers quickly.

I've been warning the guards about the murlocs. They won't listen.
I have a few ideas on how to get back at those critters. I'll need your help getting what I need for it though.
Find everything?

Give me just a minute...
It's pretty simple bait, but as long as nobody's pet gets into it, it should be safe. Just tell Jason not to eat any of it.
Poisoned bait? As long as the fish aren't going to eat it, that should work. I'll visit Remy later to pick it up.

There are precious few delights afforded to us in death. Thankfully, pain is chief among them.
You please me this day, and therefore you please the Dark Lady. Perhaps you can be of further use.
